summary: High Frontier is a brutally realistic space-exploration game built on real delta-v maps and rocket science, where you build engine/fuel/rocket card chains to physically route probes and colonists across the solar system to claim resource sites. It's punishing, fiddly, and slow to learn, but rewards players who enjoy optimizing thruster/propellant combos and reading a genuinely educational simulation of orbital mechanics.
praised: Unmatched thematic authenticity and scientific accuracy for a board game
Deep, satisfying engine-building around real rocket technology
Huge replayability from modular systems, factions, and expansions
Delta-v solar system map is a remarkable piece of design/education in itself
criticised: Extremely steep learning curve and dense rulebook
Long, fiddly turns with a lot of bookkeeping and card lookup
Can suffer from analysis paralysis and downtime between turns
Production/iconography is dense and unfriendly to newcomers

interaction.kind: site claiming and area denial, with some auction/negotiation over patents and sites

scoring.why: Victory points come from a mix of colonized/claimed sites, technology (patents), and mission completion, so the winner is whoever built the most efficient economic engine across several scoring channels
